zh: 『大人眷念故人，要调剂调剂聂仲芳，这番至意，我们当然要体仰；我想，每个月送地五十两银子薪水，仍旧在大人那里当差好了。』左宗棠一听愕然，『怎么，勉林，』他问∶『你不欢迎聂仲芳？』『不敢欺大人，聂仲芳在大人那里，亲自教导督责，他不敢越轨；到了我这里，也许会故态复萌。他是曾文正的满女婿，我不便说他，耽误了公事，大家不好。』这一说，原来有些生气的左宗棠，心平气和地问说∶『你说他「故态复萌」，请问，是什么故态？』『聂仲芳是纨绔，他比满小姐小三岁，光绪元年成婚；到光绪四年，才廿四岁，已经娶了姨太太。』『这件事我知道，他的那个早就遣走了。』左宗棠问∶『还有呢？』
en: “Your Excellency’s concern for an old friend and wish to improve Nie Zhongfang’s circumstances deserve our fullest sympathy,” Li replied. “I suggest that we send him fifty taels a month in salary while he continues to serve with you.” Zuo was astonished. “What, Mianlin? You do not want Nie Zhongfang?” “I dare not conceal the truth. Under Your Excellency’s personal instruction and supervision, he would not step out of line. Here he might revert to his old ways. As Lord Wenzheng’s youngest son-in-law, he would be difficult for me to reprimand. If public business suffered, it would be bad for everyone.” Zuo had begun to feel angry, but now asked calmly, “What old ways do you mean?” “Nie is an idle young gentleman. He is three years younger than the youngest Miss Zeng. They married in the first year of Guangxu, and by the fourth year, when he was only twenty-four, he had already taken a concubine.” “I know about that. He sent her away long ago. What else?”

zh: 『还有，曾劼刚那年奉派出使英、法两国，二小姐的故爷陈松生与聂仲芳都想跟去当随员，结果劼刚带了陈松生，没有带聂仲芳。劼刚路过上海的时候，我问他同为妹婿，何以厚此薄彼。劼刚说∶我带了他去是个累。又说∶』你看了我的日记就知道了。『李勉林又说∶』他们郎舅至亲，尚且如此，大人倒想，我怎么敢用他？『『喔，』左宗棠问∶『你看了劼刚的日记没有呢？』『看了。』『日记中怎么说？』『我录得有副本，回头送来给大人看。』『好！请你送来我看看。』
en: “When Zeng Jiegang was appointed envoy to Britain and France, both Chen Songsheng, the second daughter’s husband, and Nie wanted to accompany him as members of his staff. He took Chen but not Nie. Passing through Shanghai, he explained when I asked why he treated two brothers-in-law differently: ‘Taking him would be a burden.’ He added, ‘Read my diary and you will understand.’” Li continued, “If a close relation by marriage felt that way, Your Excellency, how could I dare employ him?” “Did you read Jiegang’s diary?” “I did.” “What did it say?” “I copied it. I shall send you the copy later.” “Good. Please let me see it.”

zh: 李勉林答应着，一回去马上将曾劼刚日记的副本，专程送到天后宫行辕。左宗棠灯下无事，细细看了一遍，其中有两条对聂规缉的批评不好，一条记于光绪四年二月十三日∶『接家报，知聂仲芳乖张已甚，季妹横被凌折，忧闷之至。』这是家务，清官难断，另外有一条记于当年九月十五日，说他不用聂仲芳的原因∶『午饭后，写一函答妹婿聂仲芳，阻其出洋之请，同为妹婿，挈松生而阻仲芳，将来必招怨恨，然而万里远行，又非余之私事，势不能徇新戚之情面，苟且迁就也。松生德器学识，朋友中实罕其匹，同行必于使事有益。仲芳年轻而纨绔习气太重，除应酬外，乃无一长，又性根无定，喜怒无常，何可携以自累，是以毅然辞之。』左宗棠心想，这不是什么不可救药的毛病。如果当时聂规缉如曾纪泽所言，现在看来却无此毛病，正好说明此人三四年以来，力矫前失，肯求上进。李勉林在制造局有许多毛病，怕落在聂规缉眼中，故而拿曾劼刚作挡箭牌，不必理他。
en: As soon as Li returned, he had the copy of Zeng Jiegang’s diary specially delivered to the Temple of the Heavenly Empress. With nothing to occupy him that evening, Zuo read it carefully by lamplight. Two entries criticized Nie Guiji. The first, dated the thirteenth day of the second month in the fourth year of Guangxu, read: “A letter from home reports that Nie Zhongfang has become exceedingly unreasonable. My youngest sister has suffered unwarranted humiliation and ill-treatment. I am deeply troubled and distressed.” This was a domestic matter, which even an upright magistrate found hard to judge. The other entry, dated the fifteenth day of the ninth month that year, explained why Zeng would not take Nie: “After luncheon, I wrote to my brother-in-law Nie Zhongfang declining his request to go abroad. To take Songsheng and refuse Zhongfang, when both are my brothers-in-law, is certain to arouse resentment. Yet this is a journey of ten thousand miles and no private undertaking of mine. I cannot give way to family feeling and make an irresponsible accommodation. Among my friends, few equal Songsheng in character, capacity, and learning. His presence will benefit the mission. Zhongfang is young and much too steeped in the habits of a pampered idler. Beyond social accomplishments, he has no particular ability. He is also unstable in temperament, with unpredictable changes of mood. How could I burden myself with him? I have therefore firmly refused.” Zuo reflected that none of these faults was incurable. If Nie had been as Zeng Jize described him then, the absence of those faults now merely showed that over the past three or four years he had worked to correct them and improve himself. Li had many failings in his management of the arsenal and feared that Nie would notice them. He was using Zeng Jiegang as a shield. There was no need to take him seriously.

zh: 主意虽定，但因第二天便须启程江宁，无法与李勉林面谈，因而亲自执笔写了一封信说∶『曾文正尝自笑坦运不佳，于诸婿中少所许可，即纪鸿亦不甚得其欢心，其所许可者，只劼刚一人，而又颇忧其聪明太露，此必有所见而云然。然吾辈待其后昆，不敢以此稍形轩轾。上年弟在京寓，目睹纪鸿苦窘情状，不觉慨然，为谋药饵之资，殡殓衣棺及还丧乡里之费，亦未尝有所歧视也。劼刚在伦敦致书言谢，却极拳拳，是于骨肉间不敢妄生爱憎厚薄之念，亦概可想。兹于仲芳，何独不然。日记云云，是劼刚一时失检，未可据为定评。』写到这里，自觉有些强词夺理；以他的地位，便是仗势欺人，所以凝神细想了一会，想出一番说得过去的道理。『传曰∶』思其人犹爱其树，君子用情，惟其厚焉「，以此言之，阁下之处仲芳不难，局员非官僚之比；局务非政事之比。仲芳能则进之，不能则撤之，其幸而无过也容之，不幸而有过则攻之讦之，俾有感奋激励之心，以生其鼓欣鼓舞、激励震惧之念，庶仲芳有所成就，不至弃为废材，而阁下有以处仲芳，即有以对曾文正矣。『左宗棠自觉这段话说得光明正大，情理周至，但意思还不足，因而又添了一段∶』弟与文正论交最早，彼此推诚相与，天下所共知；晚岁凶终隙末，亦天下所共见，然文正逝后，待文正之子若弟，及其亲友，无异文正之生存也。阁下以为然耶否耶？『
en: His mind was made up, but he had to leave for Jiangning the next day and could not discuss the matter with Li in person. He therefore wrote a letter himself: “Lord Wenzheng used to laugh at his own poor luck in sons-in-law and approved of few among them. Even Jihong did not greatly please him. Jiegang alone won his approval, yet even with him he feared that intelligence was too openly displayed. No doubt he had grounds for this judgment. We, however, must not make such distinctions in our treatment of his descendants. Last year, while staying in the capital, I saw Jihong’s distress and poverty and was deeply moved. I arranged funds for his medicines, burial clothes and coffin, and the return of his remains to his native place. I made no adverse distinction. Jiegang’s letter of thanks from London was most earnest; one may infer that he too would not lightly indulge in partiality or dislike among his own kin. Why should Zhongfang alone be an exception? What appears in the diary was a momentary lapse of discretion on Jiegang’s part and must not be taken as a final judgment.” At this point Zuo felt that he was forcing the argument. Given his position, it amounted to using authority to overbear Li. He paused in thought and devised a more defensible case. “Tradition says: ‘Remembering the man, we cherish even his tree. A gentleman’s affections should be generous.’ Viewed thus, your treatment of Zhongfang presents no difficulty. A bureau employee is not the same as a regular official, nor bureau work the same as the government of a jurisdiction. If he is capable, advance him; if incapable, remove him. If he commits no fault, allow him his place; if he does err, criticize and expose the fault. Let him feel both encouragement and warning, so that hope, resolve, and apprehension may stir him to achievement rather than leave him discarded as useless material. In treating Zhongfang thus, you will have fulfilled your obligation to Lord Wenzheng.” Zuo felt that this was forthright and reasonable, allowing fully for both principle and affection. Yet something remained to be said, and he added: “My friendship with Lord Wenzheng began very early. Our mutual sincerity was known to all; so too was our estrangement in later years. Yet since his death, I have treated his sons, his brother, and his relatives and friends exactly as I did while he lived. Do you consider that right, or not?”

zh: 送走了左宗棠，李勉林刚回制造局，便收到了左宗棠的信及送还的曾纪泽的日记。信上一篇大道理，不但坚持原意，而且隐隐责备他，不肯照顾聂规缉，反而离间人家郎舅至亲的感情，对不起曾国藩生前栽培之德。李勉林自然很不高兴。没有法子！他心里在想，不怕官，只怕管；左宗棠要派聂规缉来当会办，是他的职权，写信解释，还是客气的做法。接下来又想，左宗棠赏识聂规缉，是因为他肯说实话，而且肯留心『西学』，不用说，制造局造船造枪械，他不会是外行；不是外行又肯说实话，制造局的许多见不得人的内慕，就瞒不住了。左宗棠派此人来当会办，说不定就是专门来捉他的毛病的。
en: After seeing Zuo off, Li had scarcely returned to the arsenal when the letter arrived, together with the diary copy. Its lofty reasoning not only insisted on the original proposal but implicitly reproached him for refusing to care for Nie, sowing discord between close relations, and failing to repay Zeng’s earlier patronage. Li was naturally displeased. Yet there was nothing he could do. It was not high office that one feared, he reflected, but the authority directly over oneself. Zuo had the power to appoint Nie assistant director; writing to explain his decision was a courtesy. Then another thought occurred to him. Zuo valued Nie because he spoke honestly and attended to Western learning. He could hardly be ignorant of the arsenal’s shipbuilding and weapons manufacture. A knowledgeable man willing to speak the truth would discover its many discreditable secrets. Perhaps Zuo was sending him precisely to find fault with its director.

zh: 这样转着念头，不免心事重重，但还是得强打精神来应付，当即将亲信的文案、庶务都找了来，宣布聂规缉即将来当会办，关照文案备禀请派任的公事，措词要客气、要夸奖。然后交代庶务两件事∶第一、替会办找个宽敞的公馆，陈设布置，务求华美；第二，派专人携带三个月的薪水，到江宁去接『聂会办』夫妇来上任。这个厂务叫王伯炎，是李勉林的心腹，名为厂务，并不只管制造局的冗杂小事，他不但顾问可以干预工程及购料，甚至还是李勉林的智囊，随时可以提出建议；当然，他也是李勉林的耳目，外界对制造局的批评，一直很注意的。将李勉林交代的事，办妥了来复命时，王伯炎提到福克，『跟福克的那张合约，』他问∶『总办是打算自己跟他谈呢，还是等聂会办来谈？』『你看呢？』
en: The thought weighed upon Li, but he had to pull himself together and respond. He summoned his trusted drafting and administrative staff, announced Nie’s forthcoming appointment, and instructed the drafting officer to prepare a formal request for it, in courteous and flattering terms. He then gave the administrative officer two orders: find a spacious residence for the assistant director and furnish it splendidly; and send someone to Jiangning with three months’ salary to escort “Assistant Director Nie” and his wife to their new post. This officer, Wang Boyan, was Li’s confidant. Although nominally responsible for administrative matters, he did far more than attend to routine details. As an adviser he could intervene in engineering and purchasing, and as Li’s strategist he could offer suggestions whenever necessary. He was also Li’s eyes and ears, closely following outside criticism of the arsenal. Reporting that the arrangements had been made, he brought up Focke. “Do you intend to negotiate the contract with Focke yourself, Director, or wait for Assistant Director Nie?” “What do you think?”

zh: 『这要看总办的意思。』王伯炎说∶『各有各的好处。等聂会办来谈，好处是左大人的面子十足，聂会办也很高兴，而且，聂会办如果弄了好处，就有个把柄在总办手里，以后不怕他不就范。』『嗯、嗯！』李勉林问∶『坏处呢？』『坏处就是他不要好处。公事上是开了个例，以后这种合约都归他来谈，总办的大权旁落了。』『李勉林想了一下答说∶』他刚刚来，决不敢弄好处，不会有把柄落在我们手里；反而开了个恶例『』说得是。总办的做法也很高明，尽量跟他客气，敷衍得他舒舒服服；就是不给他实权，叫他少管公事。『』对！怎么把他敷衍得舒舒服服，就交给你办了；大不了多花几两银子，不要紧。『』是！『王伯炎答说∶』福克昨天来问道，什么时候谈合约，我说这两天左大人在这里，总办没有工夫，等左大人走了再说。现在我就通知他了，叫他马上来谈。『』好！你跟他谈。『
en: “That depends on your wishes. Each course has advantages. If we wait for Nie, His Excellency will be thoroughly gratified, and Nie will be pleased too. Moreover, if Nie takes a personal profit, you will have something to hold over him and need never fear his disobedience.” “And the disadvantage?” “That he may take no profit. Then a precedent will have been established: all such contracts will be negotiated by him, and your authority will pass into other hands.” Li considered. “Newly arrived, he certainly will not dare take anything. He will give us no hold over him; we shall merely establish an unfortunate precedent.” “Exactly. Your present course is very wise: be as courteous as possible, make him comfortable in every way, but give him no real authority and little public business to attend to.” “Yes. I leave it to you to keep him comfortable. A few extra taels do not matter.” “Very well. Focke asked yesterday when we could discuss the contract. I said that while His Excellency was here you had no time, and that we must wait until he left. I shall now tell him to come at once.” “Good. You negotiate with him.”

zh: 福克是早就预备好了的，品类、价格、交货期限，合约底稿；价格是照数量多寡决定，买得愈多愈便宜，但佣金却照比例实足计算。军火的佣金，高低不等，但最少也得一个二八扣，不过福克开的佣金，只得一个折扣；王伯炎便向翻译笑道∶『福克先生在中国多年，怎么说外行话？』『是，是佣金的折扣不对？』『不是佣金的折扣不对。』王伯炎又换了一个说法∶『是拿我们当外行看。』翻译跟福克叽哩咕噜谈了一阵，转脸向王伯炎说道∶『福克的意思是，这笔生意因为是面奉左大人交代，价钱格外克已，所以他是照成本开的，等于白当差；要请王老爷原谅。』『言重，言重！』王伯炎说∶『我们要请他原谅，这个数目，我怎么向上头交代？莫非他跟胡大先生做交易，也是这个折扣？』
en: Focke had long since prepared everything: specifications, prices, delivery dates, and a draft contract. Prices depended on quantity—the larger the purchase, the cheaper each item—but the commission was calculated at the full agreed percentage. Commissions on arms varied, though twenty per cent was the minimum. Focke, however, offered only ten. Wang Boyan smiled at the interpreter. “After so many years in China, why does Mr Focke speak like a novice?” “Is the commission rate wrong?” “No. He is treating us as novices.” The interpreter conferred with Focke for a while, then turned back. “Mr Focke says that, because His Excellency personally instructed him to undertake this transaction, he has kept the price exceptionally low. He has quoted at cost and is effectively doing the work for nothing. He asks you to understand.” “He is too kind! It is we who must ask his understanding. How am I to account to my superiors for such a figure? Does he offer Mr Hu the same rate?”

zh: 『是的，「福克居然透过翻译，这样回答；不过他也有解释，』以前如果跟胡先生自己谈。什么话都好说；倘或是跟左大人自己谈，胡先生是连一个回扣都不要的。『』唏！唷！『王伯炎大惊小怪地，』照这样说，他还算特为照应我们的？『『话也不是这么说。』翻译答说∶『据我们所知，回扣有多有少，看情形而定；好在以后还有生意，总有补报的时候。』『我是头一回，总要让我有个面子，你跟他说，我下一回补报他。』翻译跟福克又是谈了好半天，最后无可奈何地回复王伯炎，『王老爷，』他说∶『福克的意思，回扣多少都行，不过价钱要提高。』『提高到多少呢？』『这要看王老爷，要多少就是多少。』『喔，他的意思是「戴帽子」？』『是的。』
en: “Yes,” Focke actually replied through the interpreter, though he added an explanation. “When I negotiated directly with Mr Hu, any terms could be discussed. But when I dealt personally with His Excellency Zuo, Mr Hu took no rebate at all.” “Well, well!” Wang made a great show of surprise. “Then he is granting us a special favour?” “That is not quite what he means,” the interpreter answered. “As we understand it, rebates vary with circumstances. There will be more business later, and opportunities to make up for this.” “This is our first transaction. He ought to let me make a respectable showing. Tell him I shall make it up to him next time.” The interpreter spoke with Focke at length, then returned helplessly to Wang. “Mr Focke says any rebate can be arranged, but the price must rise accordingly.” “To what figure?” “That depends on you. Whatever amount you wish.” “Ah, he means to put a hat on the price?” “Yes.”

zh: 『那末戴了帽子他承认不承认呢？』『当然承认。不过┅┅』那翻译吞吞吐吐地没有再说下去。王伯炎当然要追问，『不过什么？』他说∶『大家头一回做交易，要以诚相待。』『那末，我说老实话，价目表早就开出去了。』『开给哪个？』『胡大先生。』翻译赶紧又补了一句∶『不是这两天的事。』王伯炎一听这话，大为光火；脸色青一阵、红一阵的，最后吐出一句话来∶『原来是个圈套！』
en: “And will he stand by the price with its hat on?” “Certainly. But…” The interpreter faltered. “But what?” Wang demanded. “This is our first transaction. We must be frank with each other.” “Then to be frank, the price list has already been sent out.” “To whom?” “Mr Hu.” The interpreter hastily added, “Not just within the last few days.” Wang was furious. His face went from ashen to crimson before he finally uttered the words: “So it is a trap!”

zh: 当下弄得不欢而散，王伯炎愤愤不平，再一打听，还有气人的事，原来福克决意跟胡雪岩保持良好的关系，所以在这笔军火的佣金中，为他保留了一个折扣；虽然胡雪岩表示，不愿不劳而获，但福克还是照原来的计划。买军火两成回扣，是最起码的行情，还要平白为人分去一半，王伯炎觉得这件事对总办实在很难交代。李勉林本来就有上当的感觉，在他的判断，胡雪岩将福克带到左宗棠那里，是以西征转运局委员的身份干预江南的军火采办事宜，京中的『都老爷』参上一本，连左宗棠的面子都不好看，因而叫福克来请他引见。事实上他们暗底下都谈好了，只是利用他来摆个渡而已。
en: The meeting broke up unpleasantly. Further inquiries gave the indignant Wang fresh cause for anger. Determined to preserve his good relationship with Hu, Focke had reserved a ten-per-cent share for him in the commission on this transaction. Hu had said he did not wish to profit without doing the work, but Focke persisted in his original plan. Twenty per cent was the minimum customary rebate on arms; now half of it was to be given away to someone else for nothing. Wang could scarcely explain this to his director. Li already felt he had been duped. In his view, had Hu introduced Focke to Zuo, he would have been intervening in Jiangnan arms procurement in his capacity as an officer of the Western Expedition Transport Bureau. A censor’s impeachment could have embarrassed even Zuo. That was why they had sent Focke to seek Li’s introduction. In fact, Li supposed, they had settled everything privately and merely used him to ferry the business across.

zh: 因此听到王伯炎的报告以后，认为事态很严重，特意去找上海道邵友濂商量。『合肥道赵丁忧，实在不凑巧，北洋是张振轩大有取而代之的意思；这里左湘阴着着进逼，里面一个聂仲芳卧底；外面一个胡雪岩花样百出。制造局是北洋的基础，看来要保不住了。』李勉林忧心忡忡地说∶『小村兄，你一向足智多谋，总要看在大家都是曾文正一脉相传这一点的情份上，帮帮我的忙才好。』『言重，言重。』号『小村』的邵友濂说∶『彼此休戚相关，我决无坐视之理。胡雪岩在左湘阴面前的分量，也大不如前了，你先咬咬牙撑住，等我找个机会，好好来打他一闷棍，叫他爬不起来。』『百足之虫，死而不僵。』『即使不僵也不能有什么作为了。』邵友濂打断他的话说∶『勉林兄，目前最要紧的一件事，你要把聂仲芳敷衍好。』『我明白。』『至于福克的合约，你最好还是让胡雪岩跟他去订。』『喔，这，这有什么讲究吗？』『自然有讲究。这笔经费，将来少不得要在江海关的收入之中开支；如果我这里调度不开，不是害你受人家的逼？』李勉林沉吟了一会，恍然大悟，江海关的税收归邵友濂管，将来该付福克的款子，他可以借故拖延；如果是胡雪岩跟福克签的约，福克自然只能找胡雪岩去办交涉，所以邵友濂的刁难福克，实际上便是与胡雪岩为难。『好，好！』等想通了，李勉林满口应承，『我回去就办。』
en: After Wang’s report, Li considered the matter serious enough to consult Shao Youlian, the Shanghai intendant. “Li Hongzhang’s mourning has come at a most unfortunate time. In Beiyang, Zhang Zhenxuan plainly intends to replace him. Here, Zuo advances at every step. Nie Zhongfang is planted inside, and Hu Xueyan contrives one scheme after another outside. The arsenal is the foundation of Beiyang’s strength; I fear we shall lose it.” Deeply anxious, he appealed to Shao. “Brother Xiaocun, you are always resourceful. For the sake of our common debt to Lord Wenzheng, you must help me.” “You need not speak so gravely. Our fortunes are bound together; I could never stand by. Hu carries much less weight with Zuo than he once did. Grit your teeth and hold on while I find an opportunity to strike him from behind so hard that he cannot get up again.” “A hundred-footed creature does not stiffen even in death—” “Even if it does not, it can do nothing more,” Shao interrupted. “The first priority, Brother Mianlin, is to keep Nie Zhongfang comfortable.” “I understand.” “As for Focke’s contract, you had better let Hu sign it with him.” “Is there a particular reason?” “Naturally. This money will ultimately have to come from the Shanghai Customs receipts. Suppose I cannot arrange the funds—would I not be exposing you to his demands?” After reflection, Li understood. Shao controlled the customs revenue and could make excuses to delay payment. If Hu had signed the contract, Focke could only ask Hu to intervene. By obstructing Focke, Shao would really be making difficulties for Hu. “Excellent!” Li agreed. “I shall attend to it as soon as I return.”

zh: 李勉林的办法是，命王伯炎备公事禀报左宗棠，说福克索价过高，合约谈不拢，福克以前承办西征军火，只有胡雪岩能使他就范，所以为了大局着想，请左宗棠径饬胡雪岩与福克签订合约，同时，福克原拟致送回扣一成，江南制造局决不敢领这笔回扣，请在价款中扣除，庶符涓滴归公之议。这一份『禀帖』说得冠冕党皇，到得两江总督衙门，左宗棠议为言之有理；便将原禀录了一个副本，一并寄交胡雪岩办理。这样由上海而江宁，由江宁而杭州，再由杭州而上海一个大圈子兜下来，函电往来，很快地两个月过去，事情尚无结果，局势却有了重大变化。
en: Li instructed Wang to prepare a report to Zuo stating that Focke’s price was too high and negotiations had failed. Since Focke had previously supplied the western expedition and only Hu could make him accept terms, the public interest required that Zuo order Hu directly to conclude the contract. The report added that Focke had offered a ten-per-cent rebate, which the Jiangnan Arsenal could not possibly accept; it should therefore be deducted from the price, ensuring that every last fraction went to the public treasury. This impeccably proper-sounding report reached the governor-general’s office in Jiangning. Zuo found it reasonable and sent a copy to Hu with instructions to act. Thus the affair travelled in a great circle, from Shanghai to Jiangning, from Jiangning to Hangzhou, and from Hangzhou back to Shanghai. Amid the exchange of letters and telegrams, two months quickly passed. The transaction remained unsettled, while the wider situation changed profoundly.

zh: 原来东邻朝鲜发生内乱，国王李熙暗弱，王妃闵氏当权；李熙的本生父叫李癵应，称号是『大院君』，与王妃争权，已非一日，这一次的内乱是大院君的党羽进攻王宫，伤及王妃，并杀大臣闵谦镐等人。日本见有机可乘，出兵朝鲜；驻日公使黎庶昌急电署直隶总督张树声，建议北洋立派兵舰，与日军抗衡。张树声本就想有声有色地大干一番，接到黎庶昌告警的电报，决定一面出兵观变，一面奏报朝廷。朝廷对张树声能够迅速应变，颇为嘉许，但因法国其时正在图谋越南；朝鲜又有警报，怕张树声无法应付，所以决定命在籍守制的李鸿章夺情复起，即日回津。因而便有人劝张树声说∶『朝中既已命令他主持此事，出兵似以等合肥回任后再办为宜。』张树声不听，说兵贵神速，时机一误，让日本军着了先鞭，中国要落下风。他即负北洋重任，不能因循自误。
en: Civil disorder had broken out in Korea to the east. King Yi Hui was weak, and Queen Min wielded power. The king’s own father, Yi Haeung, known as the Daewongun, had long been struggling with the queen for control. His followers now attacked the palace, wounded the queen, and killed ministers including Min Gyeom-ho. Japan seized the opportunity to send troops to Korea. Li Shuchang, China’s envoy in Japan, urgently telegraphed acting Governor-General Zhang Shusheng, recommending that Beiyang warships be dispatched immediately to counter the Japanese. Zhang had been eager for a conspicuous achievement. On receiving the warning, he decided to send troops to watch developments while simultaneously reporting to the court. The court commended his prompt response. But with France also threatening Vietnam, it feared that the Korean crisis would exceed Zhang’s capacity. Li Hongzhang was therefore ordered to interrupt his mourning at home and return to Tianjin at once. Someone advised Zhang that, since the court had appointed Li to direct the matter, he should wait until Li resumed office before sending troops. Zhang refused. Speed was essential in war; if the opportunity were lost and Japan acted first, China would be at a disadvantage. Responsible as he was for Beiyang, he could not allow indecision to lead him astray.

zh: 于是当第二道催李鸿章动身的电报刚到合肥，李鸿章已复奏即行就道，由上海转天津时，张树声所派的军队，已经在『跨海征东』途中了。张树声所派水陆两员大将，一个是北洋水师记名提督丁汝昌；一个是广东水师提督吴长庆，此人名在水师，实在是陆军，他是淮军宿将，驻扎山东登州；随带淮军六营，由登州坐招商局的轮船出海，幕府中人材济济，总理前敌营务处的，是一个年方二十四岁的江淮世家子弟，就是翰林出身、官至户部侍郎、曾为左宗棠办过粮台的哀保恒的侄子袁世凯。袁世凯从小不喜读书，虽是世家子弟，行为无赖，不齿于乡党。在家乡存不住身，异想天开，召集了无业少年十余人，由河南项城到山东烟台，将同伴留在旅舍中，只身去见吴长庆。吴长庆当时以广东水师提督办理山东军务，他跟袁世凯的嗣父袁保庆是八拜之交，对故人之子，当然要照应，首先动问来意。
en: Thus, when the second telegram urging Li to depart had only just reached Hefei, and Li had replied that he would leave immediately for Tianjin by way of Shanghai, Zhang’s expedition was already crossing the sea eastward. Its naval and military commanders were Ding Ruchang, a Beiyang naval officer registered for appointment as commander-in-chief, and Wu Changqing, nominally commander-in-chief of the Guangdong navy but in practice a land commander. Wu was a veteran of the Huai Army stationed at Dengzhou in Shandong. He sailed from there in China Merchants’ steamers with six battalions. His headquarters contained many able men. Directing the field military administration was a twenty-four-year-old from an established Jianghuai family: Yuan Shikai, nephew of Yuan Baoheng, the former Hanlin scholar who had risen to vice-minister of revenue and managed supplies for Zuo. Yuan Shikai had disliked study from childhood. Despite his distinguished family, his disreputable behaviour had made him an outcast among his neighbours. Unable to remain at home, he conceived an extraordinary plan: gathering more than ten unemployed youths, he travelled from Xiangcheng in Henan to Yantai in Shandong. Leaving his companions at an inn, he went alone to see Wu. Wu, then handling military affairs in Shandong under his Guangdong naval title, had been a sworn brother of Yuan’s adoptive father, Yuan Baoqing. He naturally wished to help his old friend’s son and first asked what had brought him there.
